claims.finding: In the 8-K accepted 2026-07-31T21:28:25Z (items 2.05, 5.02, 7.01) ChargePoint reaffirmed Q2 revenue guidance of $100-110m for the quarter ending 2026-07-31 - i.e. on the final day of that quarter - and simultaneously disclosed a 10% workforce reduction with only ~$6m of restructuring cost that it expects to complete in Q3 FY2027, putting the charge in the next quarter rather than the one being reported, yet the stock fell 12.77% in the five sessions into the print with zero SEC filings in the whole of August 2026 and no captured news after 2026-08-27.
claims.corpus_ref: filings.json accession 0001777393-26-000057 (form 8-K, items 2.05,5.02,7.01, accepted 2026-07-31T21:28:25Z, primary_document chpt-20260728.htm); the guidance-reaffirmation quote and the 10%/$6m figures are in docs/873be191fea4f318e7bcd6728893513945a3f67f.txt lines 142-148 (StockTwits sweep 20260830T083857Z)
claims.why_not_priced: Reaffirming revenue guidance on the last day of the quarter is close to a pre-announcement, and the restructuring cost being scheduled for Q3 means the reported quarter's cost base is unaffected. Nobody aggregated that: this name has 88 captured items of which 86 are EDGAR index rows, only one third-party post in the corpus noticed the reaffirmation at all, and there is no analyst preview, no consensus figure and no sell-side note anywhere in the capture. If the market had priced a de-risked revenue line and a deferred charge, the stock would not have lost 12.77% in five sessions on no filing and no news; instead the tape looks like generic small-cap EV-charging risk-off into an event.
claims.independence: A separate filing points the same way on the corporate-action axis rather than the P&L: the 8-K accepted 2026-06-30T20:32:30Z (accession 0001777393-26-000047, item 5.02) amended the CEO severance agreement to remove its termination date and extend it until the CEO's departure, https://www.rapidticker.com/news/chpt-sec-filing-d6f419 - which is the kind of housekeeping done ahead of a change of control and matches the corpus's heavy unsolicited M&A speculation, though on its own it is inference not evidence.
